# User Manual & Technical Documentation: Interactive Sheaf & Hodge Dashboard

This document serves as a comprehensive guide for peer reviewers, researchers, and students to operate and understand the **Interactive Sheaf & Hodge Dashboard** (index.html). The dashboard visually and numerically demonstrates the theoretical pillars of the paper: _"The Persistent Hodge Decomposition of Cellular Sheaves: Algebraic Stability, Spectral Properties, and Generalization in Topological Deep Learning"_.

## 1\. Executive Summary & Core Objective

The interactive dashboard bridges abstract algebraic topology (cellular sheaves, sheaf Laplacians, and Hodge decompositions) with tangible, real-time numerical and physical simulations. By providing a sandbox to manipulate initial cochain signals, modify sheaf restriction morphisms, and simulate continuous-time ordinary differential equations (ODEs), users can physically witness:

- **Perfect Hodge Orthogonality (Theorem 4.1):** Verification of orthogonal projections at machine precision limit (![](data:image/png;base64,)).
- **Exponential Dirichlet Energy Decay (Theorem 4.2):** Exponential convergence of continuous sheaf diffusion flows governed strictly by the algebraic connectivity/spectral gap (![](data:image/png;base64,)).
- **Over-smoothing Mitigation (Section 6.4):** Contrastive comparison showing standard low-pass Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) collapsing representations versus Anisotropic Orthogonal Sheaves preserving linear class boundaries.
- **Hardware Feasibility (Section 6.5 & Table 2):** Memory and speed latency trade-offs on microcontrollers of varying architectures.

### A. Header Bar

- **Status Badge:** Confirms math verification status ("Math Sim Verified").
- **GitHub Redirection:** Dedicated button to link directly to your open-source research workspace.

### B. Left Panel (Controls & Parameters)

- **Stage 1 (Setup & Sheaf Topology):** Contains selectors for graph structures and local restriction mapping models.
- **Stage 2 (Diffusion Simulation):** Controls for the Euler ODE solver, time step (![](data:image/png;base64,)) variables, and the angle slider to manipulate individual vertex cochain states.

### C. Center Panel (Live Geometric Attractor)

- An interactive SVG canvas displaying node states, adjacency links, and direction arrows representing the active cochains.
- **Dynamic Node Selection:** Clicking any node highlights it with an emerald glow and binds its state directly to the left panel slider for custom modifications.

### D. Right Panel (Mathematical Metrics & Visual Feedback)

- **Live Mathematical Monitors:** Reports real-time Hodge orthogonality limits and the theoretical spectral gap (![](data:image/png;base64,)).
- **Real-time Convergence Log:** Plots the generalized Dirichlet energy of the signal over time on a logarithmic scale.

### E. Lower Panel (Embedded Silicon Profiler)

- Reproduces and expands the microcontroller benchmarks presented in Table 2, showcasing compiled footprint scaling as a function of the signal window size ![](data:image/png;base64,).

## 3\. Detailed Interactive Functions & Workflows

### 3.1. Topology & Functor Configurations (Stage 1)

- **Cycle Graph ![](data:image/png;base64,) vs Bipartite ![](data:image/png;base64,):** \* Selecting **Cycle Graph ![](data:image/png;base64,)** initializes an undirected ring containing 6 nodes, where each vertex stalk represents a ![](data:image/png;base64,) vector space (![](data:image/png;base64,)).
  - Selecting **Bipartite ![](data:image/png;base64,)** generates a fully connected bipartite graph where node states are evaluated as scalars (![](data:image/png;base64,)).
- **Anisotropic Orthogonal Sheaf vs Isotropic Identity Sheaf:**
  - **Anisotropic (Orthogonal):** Equips the graph with orthogonal rotation restriction maps (![](data:image/png;base64,)). On the bipartite graph, this is simulated using contrasting sign-flips (![](data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAABQAAAAfCAYAAADnTu3OAAAAfUlEQVR4AeySMQqAMAxFVboU3aSDFOypPIBncvFKHqNZs7pH6RTo1MRFSOHDJ5AHeXToPn4G1As1h+ZQYOA/36aPMc4ppaU1IYSJmyknv8PROXcS0dUa7/1eARHxzjlvALAKclRAPtD2crIWwvcNyG3IujmUeeNb5pDbkPUHAAD//1b+SyoAAAAGSURBVAMAgcRnP+n7VPEAAAAASUVORK5CYII=) or ![](data:image/png;base64,)) across the heterophilic edge boundary to represent adjacent opposing classes.
  - **Isotropic (Identity):** Forces all restriction maps to equal the Identity matrix (![](data:image/png;base64,)), matching trivial, symmetric graph message passing.

### 3.2. Real-Time Signal Modification

When the **Cycle Graph ![](data:image/png;base64,)** is active:

- Click on any of the numbered nodes (![](data:image/png;base64,) to ![](data:image/png;base64,)) on the center canvas.
- Observe that the selected node is highlighted with an emerald halo, and the left slider updates to show its current vector angle.
- Slide the **Vector Angle (Degrees)** controller. The vector arrow on the active node will rotate immediately, updating its coordinates:  
   ![](data:image/png;base64,)
- Use this control to manually introduce high-frequency components or customized irregularities in the starting cochain.

### 3.3. Running Sheaf Diffusion (Stage 2)

- Click **Run ODE** to initiate the discrete Euler approximation of the continuous-time diffusion flow:  
   ![](data:image/png;base64,)
- **Observation (Isotropic Sheaf):** If the _Identity Sheaf_ is active, the vectors on ![](data:image/png;base64,) will rapidly collapse in length and align in an identical direction, or flatten to ![](data:image/png;base64,) on the heterophilic ![](data:image/png;base64,) graph (representing representation collapse/over-smoothing).
- **Observation (Anisotropic Sheaf):** If the _Orthogonal Sheaf_ is active, the vectors will rotate dynamically and converge to a stable, non-trivial harmonic configuration, preserving distinct differences between opposing classes.
- **Log Chart Feedback:** As the ODE runs, the line chart on the right panel records the decay of Dirichlet energy. Under positive algebraic connectivity (![](data:image/png;base64,)), the chart plots a straight downward slope, proving **exponential convergence (Theorem 4.2)**.

### 3.4. Silicon Footprint Profiling (Lower Panel)

- Navigate to the **Microcontroller Hardware Profiling Simulator**.
- Select **32 Samples** or **64 Samples** from the dropdown menu.
- The simulator evaluates the computational complexity of running the ![](data:image/png;base64,)\-TDA filtration over the selected window size:

  - Selecting ![](data:image/png;base64,) **Samples** simulates the exponential organizational scaling of simplicial coordinates. Observe how SRAM allocations on the _Cortex-M7_ jump to ![](data:image/png;base64,) KB, and execution time increases to ![](data:image/png;base64,) ms, demonstrating the combinatorial limits of deploying topological pipelines at the deep edge.

## 4\. Mathematical Mapping to the Manuscript

To verify your manuscript's analytical results using this dashboard, refer to the following key mappings:

- **Theorem 4.1 (Persistent Sheaf Hodge Decomposition):** Observe the **Hodge Orthogonality** value under _Spectral Statistics_ on the right panel. It evaluates to ![](data:image/png;base64,), proving that the orthogonal projection of any modified cochain signal onto the gradient and harmonic kernel spaces is exact down to double-precision machine limits.
- **Theorem 4.2 (Convergence to Harmonic Space):** Run the diffusion ODE. The exponential convergence rate plotted on the logarithmic decay line chart is strictly proportional to the displayed **Spectral Gap (![](data:image/png;base64,))** value. Under identity configuration, the gap drops to ![](data:image/png;base64,), showing why trivial graph low-pass filters fail to prevent representation collapse.
